name: Sheraton Maui Resort & Spa
positioning: Oceanfront resort on 23 acres of Kaanapali Beach, right beside Pu'u Keka'a (Black Rock) on Maui
best_for: Snorkelers who want reef and sea turtles right in front of the resort
Families wanting a suite that sleeps up to 5 and a pool with a children's area

facts.text: The resort is oceanfront on Kaanapali Beach, right beside Pu'u Keka'a (Black Rock).
The resort is set on 23 acres.
The resort has six wings: Anuenue, Lahaina, Hoku, Nalu, Moana and Ohana.
Every room has a balcony, terrace or lanai.
The Ohana Suite is the resort's family suite, with a pull-out bed and a Murphy bed to sleep up to 5 people.
The nightly cliff dive honors Kahekili, the last chief of Maui, who leapt from Pu'u Keka'a's sacred promontory.
The Spa at Black Rock uses natural products drawing on ocean plants and Polynesian essential oils.
Spa massages include Hawaiian Lomi Lomi and a Pu'u Keka'a Hot Stone massage.
Cultural activities rotate monthly and include koi fish feeding, lei making, ukulele lessons and hula dancing.
Guests can roast s'mores at oceanfront fire pits at sunset.
At Teppan-yaki Dan, chefs prepare lobster, steak and more in front of guests.
The Kaanapali Golf Courses, with 36 holes, are steps from the hotel.

highlights.text: Guests can see tropical marine life, coral reefs and honu, green sea turtles, in the waters right in front of the resort.
A cliff dive ceremony takes place every evening at sunset, a tradition since the resort first opened.

The Moana wing sits atop Pu'u Keka'a (Black Rock); its one-bedroom oceanfront suites have a private wraparound balcony with views of the Kaanapali coastline, Black Rock's coral reef and the islands of Lanai and Molokai.
The lagoon-style pool has several large swimming areas linked by lava-rock waterways, a small waterslide and a shallow children's area.
Over 80% of the rooms offer ocean views.

considerations.text: The resort is spread out, so room location is worth choosing carefully.
The cliff dive does not take place in inclement weather.
WhataHotel notes it is a large resort property with potential for crowds.
